title: The top US cities in 2026
gist: Oxford Economics' 2026 Global Cities Index has US cities holding half the top 10 and 30 of the top 100, driven by GDP, headquarters and tech-led GDP per person (16 of the top 20). A new 'Cities to Watch' list flags Boise, Durham, Jacksonville and San Antonio as emerging growth metros.

themes.theme: US dominance of Global Cities Index

insights.claim: US cities account for half of the top 10 and 30 of the top 100 cities in Oxford Economics' 2026 Global Cities Index, with strong Economics scores separating them from the rest of the world.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Confirms concentration of global urban economic weight in US metros; supports overweight US regional exposure.
insights.quote: Strong Economics scores are what set US cities apart from the rest of the global economy.

insights.claim: The 90 US cities in the GCI (9% of the 1,000 analysed) generate a third of the composite GDP, with average GDP per capita of $101,000, close to four times the GCI weighted city average.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Highlights outsized productivity of US metros versus global peers.

insights.claim: US cities' Human Capital scores are high because they host 21% of GCI corporate headquarters, plus top universities and high educational attainment.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: HQ and university clustering is a durable moat for talent and high-value jobs.

insights.claim: New York ranks first overall and in Economics, with a GDP score 20% above the next-highest city, Tokyo, and strong Human Capital and Quality of Life.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: New York remains the single largest urban economy in the index.
insights.locator: Foremost in the Global City Index rankings

insights.claim: The top 10 US cities in the 2026 GCI are New York, Seattle, San Francisco, Boston, San Jose, Los Angeles, Washington DC, Dallas, Houston and Atlanta.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Reference list of leading US metros for regional allocation screens.
insights.locator: Top 10 US cities in 2026 Global Cities Index

themes.theme: Tech and specialisation drive GDP per person

insights.claim: Tech-heavy metros San Jose, San Francisco and Seattle stand out, with high GDP per person from large tech sectors that in turn spurs consistently strong GDP growth.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Tech concentration links to income per capita and growth; regional exposure to tech is a growth lever.
insights.quote: Leading US cities generate high GDP per person, which in turn spurs consistently strong GDP growth.
insights.locator: Foremost in the Global City Index rankings / Chart 3 paragraph

insights.claim: Boston's top-10 ranking is buoyed by life sciences, pharmaceuticals and finance rather than tech alone.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Shows a non-tech route to high urban productivity.

insights.claim: US cities hold 16 of the top 20 spots for GDP per person (80%); only smaller, specialised cities like Dublin, Basel, Luxembourg and Zurich break in.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: US productivity per head is hard to match among large cities.

themes.theme: Cities to Watch: emerging growth metros

insights.claim: The new 'Cities to Watch' list names Boise, Durham, Jacksonville and San Antonio as US cities with steady job, GDP and population growth, aided by strong post-Covid in-migration.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Candidate secondary metros for regional growth, real estate and labour-market exposure.
insights.locator: Several US cities are emerging as growth leaders

insights.claim: In-migration to these four cities was driven by outdoor amenities, and they score better on Environment metrics than larger peers.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Amenity-driven migration shapes where population growth flows.
insights.locator: Several US cities are emerging as growth leaders

insights.claim: Boise and Durham attract young people via large universities that foster entrepreneurship; Boise's tech growth is helped by Micron, which is undergoing a $50 billion expansion.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Micron's $50bn expansion is a local demand driver for Boise; watch semis capex.
insights.locator: Boise and Durham have especially drawn

insights.claim: Durham's growth is concentrated in life sciences and pharma near Research Triangle Park, shared with Raleigh.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.locator: Boise and Durham have especially drawn

insights.claim: Jacksonville's growth is led by fintech alongside finance, federal government and tourism, while San Antonio's growth is diversified across military, defence contractors, auto manufacturing, finance and tourism.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Diversified bases make these cities resilient growth stories.

themes.theme: Rank movers and Human Capital versus size

insights.claim: Biggest GCI ranking climbers include Greenville (SC), Charleston, Provo, Fresno and Indianapolis, driven by steady economic growth and improved Human Capital metrics such as headquarters and educational attainment.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Signals where relative momentum is building outside the coastal giants.

insights.claim: Biggest GCI ranking decliners include New Orleans, Rochester (NY), Albany (NY), Hartford and Pittsburgh.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Relative laggards may face weaker growth and fiscal pressure.

insights.claim: Smaller cities score lower on Economics due to size but tend to do better on Human Capital because of universities, educational attainment and age profiles; Provo, Durham, Worcester, Madison and Des Moines score among the highest.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Size and human capital are separate axes when screening cities.
insights.locator: Smaller cities that rank lower on the Economics score

insights.claim: El Paso, Columbia (SC), Stockton and New Haven have weaker Human Capital but healthy GDP growth and good economic diversity scores; large anchor employers (federal government, state government, Amazon, Yale) boost their economic stability scores.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Anchor employers give stability but create concentration exposure.
insights.locator: Other smaller cities, such as El Paso

insights.claim: High US labour mobility forces cities to compete for migrants and jobs, which sets the US apart from cross-continental peers and supports continued productivity and GDP growth.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Competition for talent underpins US urban outperformance over time.
insights.quote: which often forces cities to compete for migrants and jobs, sets it apart from its cross-continental peers
insights.locator: The findings show that every US city has a unique profile

insights.claim: Oxford Economics expects US cities to keep generating stellar productivity and GDP growth, keeping them at the top of the economic pyramid.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Base case supports long-run overweight of US metro economies.
insights.locator: The findings show that every US city has a unique profile
